newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds trade narrowly, seek direction.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds trade narrowly, seek direction.

text.p: Argentine bonds dipped slightly in medium-volume trade late morning Friday in a market split between optimists and pessimists, analysts said.

"The U.S. long bond is without major news," said one trader at an international bank. "Market values are trading narrowly, but volume is substantial. That tells me there are enough people seeing this market from opposed perspectives."
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was unchanged at 90 3/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional dipped $0.10 to 125.90.

Another trader said that next week's U.S. indicators will help define interest rates there, giving cues to local traders. He agreed the market was split down the middle "with enough traders seeing prices up and others seeing prices down to encourage a healthy volume of trade."
He added he expected the market to find a more definite direction next week.
